title: Payments & Finance Note — Capturing and Applying Pre-Orders & Back-Orders Deposits
content:
**Basis.** A Pre-Orders & Back-Orders deposit is captured once, at reservation, by card. At shipment the deposit is applied in full to the fulfilment order. The customer then pays the balance on the fulfilment order, where every order tender may be used. The balance is the final unit price times the quantity, less the deposit, plus tax. A deposit is applied only once the reservation is in status fulfilled. A lower final price never reduces the deposit below what was paid: it lowers only the balance. When the deposit exceeds the final price, the difference is refunded to the card at shipment.

**Deposit movements on a reservation's history**

| Moment | Movement | Tender |
|---|---|---|
| Reservation | Deposit charged, once | Card |
| Shipment (reservation fulfilled) | Deposit applied in full to the fulfilment order | — |
| Shipment, where the deposit exceeds the final price | Difference refunded | The card the deposit came from |

**Status condition.** The deposit is applied only when the reservation shows fulfilled. While a reservation is reserved, awaiting consent, in production or allocated, its deposit is held and not yet applied.

**Worked illustration (hypothetical Deposit Pre-Order of one unit with a $60.00 deposit)**

- Final unit price $300.00. The deposit of $60.00 is applied in full, and the balance is $300.00 less $60.00, which is $240.00, plus tax. Any order tender may pay it.
- Final unit price lowered to $280.00 before shipment. The deposit stays at $60.00 and the balance falls to $220.00, plus tax.
- Final unit price of $50.00. The deposit of $60.00 exceeds the final price, so the difference of $10.00 is refunded to the card at shipment.
